context.guidance: Store Authentication Secrets with a current, salted, deliberately slow password hashing function, never with a plain or fast unsalted digest. Re-hash each existing record with the new function the next time the Data Principal authenticates. Rule 6(1)(a) requires protection of the Personal Data these secrets guard, and a weak hash removes that protection once the store is read.

value.fix: Stop storing security answers with security.hmac(answer). HMAC is a fast hash with one static key and no per-record salt, so anyone who can read the table can brute-force the answers quickly, and identical answers produce identical hashes. Use a slow, salted password hash such as argon2id (memory >= 19 MiB, iterations >= 2) or bcrypt (cost >= 12). Hashing is async, so remove the synchronous setter in the SecurityAnswer model and hash in beforeCreate/beforeUpdate hooks instead, normalising first: `SecurityAnswer.beforeSave(async (rec) => { if (rec.changed('answer')) rec.answer = await argon2.hash(rec.answer.trim().toLowerCase(), { type: argon2.argon2id }) })`. Make sure the answer column can hold the longer self-describing hash string. In the reset-password flow, replace the equality check `security.hmac(answer) === data.answer` with `await argon2.verify(data.answer, submitted.trim().toLowerCase())`. To migrate old records, check whether the stored value starts with '$argon2' (or '$2b$' for bcrypt). If it doesn't, it is a legacy HMAC: compare it with crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(security.hmac(submitted)), Buffer.from(stored)), and on success immediately save the argon2id hash of the submitted answer over it. Records whose owner never authenticates should be invalidated after a set deadline, so users must re-enrol their security answer. Add rate limiting or lockout on the answer check, and test that new answers are stored as argon2id, that a correct legacy answer is upgraded, and that wrong answers are rejected.
